voice.refText: Twice a week, you sell your plasma, the pale part of your blood. It's the most the law allows. That's the band. A thin strip you wear across your forehead. While you sleep, it lends your brain to a company. And it pays you, by the hour.

Waitress.describe: A quick, bright female mezzo: a diner waitress in her thirties. Dry, wry and fast, a pencil-behind-the-ear voice that has heard every excuse, flat American vowels, a smile under the sarcasm.

Marco.describe: A young, warm male tenor: a short-order cook in his late twenties. Slightly hoarse, easygoing and quick to laugh, cheeky, a little breathless, a working man's casual American English.

Plant boss.describe: A big, booming male baritone: a car-plant boss in his fifties. Confident and loud, a salesman's warmth, quick to laugh at his own jokes, a voice used to talking over machinery.

Banker.describe: A smooth, precise male tenor: a small-town bank manager in his sixties. Polite, slightly pompous, every consonant crisp, a man pleased to correct you.

Mayor.describe: A clear, ringing female alto: a small-town mayor in her fifties. Warm and public, a speech-giver's lift on every line, upbeat and a little too sure of herself.

Rival.describe: A low, gravelly female voice: a diner owner in her sixties across town. Husky, blunt and sardonic, slow and knowing, a smoker's rasp, never impressed.

Plumber.describe: A deep, slow male bass: a plumber in his forties. Unhurried, stubborn and amused, few words and every one final, a man who knows nobody else can fix the sink.

Reporter.describe: A bright, fast female soprano: a local TV reporter in her twenties. Eager and clipped, a broadcaster's projection, every question pitched up like a headline.

lines.text: What if you fired everyone and hired AI?
lines.say: [sly, close, a dare with a grin behind it] What if you fired everyone and hired AI?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Waitress: Marco's sick. Again.
lines.say: [flat, fed up, holding the phone out like a bad fish] Marco's sick. Again.
lines.speaker: Waitress

lines.text: Marco: Fourth Monday. I know. I know.
lines.say: [croaky, guilty, a fake cough between the sentences] Fourth Monday. I know. I know.
lines.speaker: Marco

lines.text: Waitress: Is it on the payroll?
lines.say: [stunned, small, the phone forgotten on the floor] Is it on the payroll?
lines.speaker: Waitress

lines.text: It is not.
lines.say: [dry, delighted, a secret] It is not.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So what if you could hire a machine for any job in town, for nothing at all?
lines.say: [quick, conspiratorial, the last four words savoured] So what if you could hire a machine for any job in town, for nothing at all?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Six weeks from now you'll be the richest person this town has ever had. And its last customer.
lines.say: [grand, relishing it, then a beat and the last sentence low and cold] Six weeks from now you'll be the richest person this town has ever had. And its last customer.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Every lunch, the same count. The whistle. Forty stools full.
lines.say: [brisk, fond, counting on fingers, satisfied on the last word] Every lunch, the same count. The whistle. Forty stools full.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You have never once wondered where the overalls get the money.
lines.say: [teasing, slow, a finger wagged at you] You have never once wondered where the overalls get the money.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The rule. Three lines.
lines.say: [clear, clipped, a card laid on the table] The rule. Three lines.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Type a job. By the next shift a machine worker is at your door. No wage. No sleep. No mistakes.
lines.say: [exact, brisk, each of the last three a hammer tap] Type a job. By the next shift a machine worker is at your door. No wage. No sleep. No mistakes.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Hire as many as you like. Rent them to anyone who asks.
lines.say: [sly, generous, a shopkeeper opening the doors] Hire as many as you like. Rent them to anyone who asks.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And the app has one dial. What a shift costs whoever rents it. Only you can turn it. Remember that.
lines.say: [measured, slower, the last two words almost a whisper] And the app has one dial. What a shift costs whoever rents it. Only you can turn it. Remember that.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Waitress: What's it eat?
lines.say: [curious, suspicious, leaning in close to the screen] What's it eat?
lines.speaker: Waitress

lines.text: Nobody answers that. Hold on to it.
lines.say: [low, knowing, a pin pushed into the map] Nobody answers that. Hold on to it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And Marco's cough clears up the second he hears the word robot. He's on his way in.
lines.say: [amused, quick, a laugh under the first sentence] And Marco's cough clears up the second he hears the word robot. He's on his way in.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Marco: Who's this?
lines.say: [out of breath, outraged, a burger sailing over his head] Who's this?
lines.speaker: Marco

lines.text: Marco: It can't even taste it!
lines.say: [wounded, shouting, burger still on his hat] It can't even taste it!
lines.speaker: Marco

lines.text: You fire all three before the rush. Marco, your waitress, and the dishwasher who left last year and never came back anyway.
lines.say: [brisk, ruthless, a shrug of a joke on the last clause] You fire all three before the rush. Marco, your waitress, and the dishwasher who left last year and never came back anyway.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It's true, by the way. In 2018 a burger-flipping robot called Flippy started work at a restaurant in Pasadena, California.
lines.say: [an aside, amused, the fact quick and plain, a wink on California] It's true, by the way. In twenty eighteen a burger-flipping robot called Flippy started work at a restaurant in Pasadena, California.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your first napkin. Three wages gone, burgers the same. Money out is money out. Simple.
lines.say: [pleased with yourself, counting it off, the last word smug] Your first napkin. Three wages gone, burgers the same. Money out is money out. Simple.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Forty stools fed in the time Marco took to find his hat.
lines.say: [quick, gleeful, a dig on the last word] Forty stools fed in the time Marco took to find his hat.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plant boss: Where'd you get the cooks?
lines.say: [mouth half full, amazed, a man who smells money] Where'd you get the cooks?
lines.speaker: Plant boss

lines.text: And the plant across the road has four hundred people in it.
lines.say: [slow, a hook sinking in, the number weighed] And the plant across the road has four hundred people in it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The boss rents fifty for the paint shop. The dial says cheap. Your phone pings once a shift. You sleep with it under your pillow and it pings through the feathers.
lines.say: [building, greedy, each ping a little faster, a grin on the feathers] The boss rents fifty for the paint shop. The dial says cheap. Your phone pings once a shift. You sleep with it under your pillow and it pings through the feathers.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plant boss: They don't stop for lunch?
lines.say: [dazed, checking his watch, barely believing it] They don't stop for lunch?
lines.speaker: Plant boss

lines.text: They don't stop for anything.
lines.say: [deadpan, cool, a complete thought] They don't stop for anything.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In 1865 the economist Jevons wrote that burning coal more efficiently did not cut the coal that got burned. The very contrary. Cheaper means more.
lines.say: [leaning in, a lesson with relish, the last three words slow and pointed] In eighteen sixty-five the economist Jevons wrote that burning coal more efficiently did not cut the coal that got burned. The very contrary. Cheaper means more.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So the boss runs three shifts where he ran one. And rents five hundred.
lines.say: [quick, escalating, a gasp of a laugh on the number] So the boss runs three shifts where he ran one. And rents five hundred.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: His napkin. Your sum. Same line missing.
lines.say: [dry, ominous, the last sentence a secret kept from the room] His napkin. Your sum. Same line missing.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Marco: Got hired here!
lines.say: [beaming, shouting across the road, hard hat sideways] Got hired here!
lines.speaker: Marco

lines.text: Marco: Again?
lines.say: [small, crushed, the hat in his hands] Again?
lines.speaker: Marco

lines.text: Again. And the bank manager walks in asking who built your kitchen.
lines.say: [flat on the first word, then brisk, the story moving on] Again. And the bank manager walks in asking who built your kitchen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Banker: ATMs didn't kill tellers, you know.
lines.say: [smug, glasses up, a man quoting the one book he read] ATMs didn't kill tellers, you know.
lines.speaker: Banker

lines.text: He's right. From 1980 to 2010, as cash machines spread across America, bank tellers rose modestly, from about 500,000 to about 550,000.
lines.say: [fair, even, conceding the point with a raised eyebrow] He's right. From nineteen eighty to twenty ten, as cash machines spread across America, bank tellers rose modestly, from about five hundred thousand to about five hundred and fifty thousand.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The machine counted the cash. It never asked about your mother's hip.
lines.say: [warm, wry, the second sentence softer] The machine counted the cash. It never asked about your mother's hip.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He rents twelve. They ask about mothers' hips.
lines.say: [deadpan, a trap snapping shut, a laugh held under it] He rents twelve. They ask about mothers' hips.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mayor: New jobs always come.
lines.say: [bright, practised, a sash and a wave] New jobs always come.
lines.speaker: Mayor

lines.text: They did. In 1900 about 41 percent of American workers were on farms. By 2000, under 2 percent. People were still better at something.
lines.say: [steady, granting it, then a turn on the last sentence, the last word stressed] They did. In nineteen hundred about forty-one percent of American workers were on farms. By two thousand, under two percent. People were still better at something.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Here, you type the new job in.
lines.say: [sly, quiet, a card turned over] Here, you type the new job in.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rival: Don't tell my customers.
lines.say: [hushed, guilty, signing fast at her own door] Don't tell my customers.
lines.speaker: Rival

lines.text: Your competition pays you rent.
lines.say: [gloating, quick, a laugh held under it] Your competition pays you rent.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Every owner in town, the same napkin. Nobody copied. Nobody had to.
lines.say: [cool, a fan of cards laid out, the last three words slow] Every owner in town, the same napkin. Nobody copied. Nobody had to.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plumber: I'm not typing my own job in.
lines.say: [gruff, amused, pushing the phone back with one finger] I'm not typing my own job in.
lines.speaker: Plumber

lines.text: The plumber won't. The hairdresser won't. Everyone else is in the app by Friday.
lines.say: [brisk, ticking them off, a shrug on the last sentence] The plumber won't. The hairdresser won't. Everyone else is in the app by Friday.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Reporter: The town's first machine millionaire!
lines.say: [breathless, thrilled, microphone thrust forward] The town's first machine millionaire!
lines.speaker: Reporter

lines.text: And six Fridays in, the plant pays its last human wage.
lines.say: [quiet, cold, the last three words spaced out] And six Fridays in, the plant pays its last human wage.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The key to the town. A convoy, off to the next town. Your till hums.
lines.say: [grand, giddy, drunk on it, humming the last word] The key to the town. A convoy, off to the next town. Your till hums.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Reporter: Isn't this the dream? Nobody has to work.
lines.say: [bright, earnest, half a question to the camera] Isn't this the dream? Nobody has to work.
lines.speaker: Reporter

lines.text: Someone thought so. In 1930 the economist Keynes named it: technological unemployment, jobs lost because we save labour faster than we find new uses for it. A temporary phase, he called it. And in about a hundred years, about now, he guessed, a fifteen-hour week.
lines.say: [storyteller, measured, the name given with relish, a knowing lift on about now] Someone thought so. In nineteen thirty the economist Keynes named it: technological unemployment, jobs lost because we save labour faster than we find new uses for it. A temporary phase, he called it. And in about a hundred years, about now, he guessed, a fifteen-hour week.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He meant the hours shared out and the pay kept. Here, the hours went to the machines. The pay went to you.
lines.say: [even, then pointed, the last word landed on you like a finger] He meant the hours shared out and the pay kept. Here, the hours went to the machines. The pay went to you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Forty stools. Nobody on them. Problem one. The overalls were your wages.
lines.say: [hollow, slow, counting the empty room, the last sentence a cold realisation] Forty stools. Nobody on them. Problem one. The overalls were your wages.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Marco ate here. So did the paint shop. So did twelve tellers.
lines.say: [quiet, each name a stool going empty, a sad laugh on the tellers] Marco ate here. So did the paint shop. So did twelve tellers.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You saved every wage you paid. You lost a slice of every wage in town.
lines.say: [exact, slow, the sum done out loud, the last word a thud] You saved every wage you paid. You lost a slice of every wage in town.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Two economists wrote this sum down this year, Hemenway Falk and Tsoukalas: "The AI Layoff Trap". Each firm keeps the whole saving and bears only a slice of the spending it destroys; the rest lands on its rivals. One model, not yet checked by other economists. Your napkin got there first.
lines.say: [clear, a fact told as a reveal, honest on the caveat, a proud grin on the last sentence] Two economists wrote this sum down this year, Hemenway Falk and Tsoukalas: "The AI Layoff Trap". Each firm keeps the whole saving and bears only a slice of the spending it destroys; the rest lands on its rivals. One model, not yet checked by other economists. Your napkin got there first.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Money out was never out. It was going round.
lines.say: [low, slow, a lesson landing, the last word drawn out] Money out was never out. It was going round.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You didn't fire a cook. You fired a customer who happened to know how to cook.
lines.say: [quiet, a blade of a line, the second sentence slower and plain] You didn't fire a cook. You fired a customer who happened to know how to cook.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: An old story, a union leader's own, Walter Reuther's. A car-plant manager showed him a hall of machines and asked how he'd collect union dues from them. He asked how the manager would get them to buy cars.
lines.say: [storyteller, warm, savouring the set-up, the punchline dry and unhurried] An old story, a union leader's own, Walter Reuther's. A car-plant manager showed him a hall of machines and asked how he'd collect union dues from them. He asked how the manager would get them to buy cars.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You're the manager. Marco's the one outside the glass.
lines.say: [pointed, soft, the second sentence almost gentle] You're the manager. Marco's the one outside the glass.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Not a new sum, either. In 1914 Henry Ford doubled his workers' pay to five dollars a day, and wrote later that his own sales depended, in a measure, on the wages he paid.
lines.say: [wry, plain, a fact that should have been obvious, a shrug at the end] Not a new sum, either. In nineteen fourteen Henry Ford doubled his workers' pay to five dollars a day, and wrote later that his own sales depended, in a measure, on the wages he paid.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rival: You stop first.
lines.say: [sharp, cornered, phone still in her hand] You stop first.
lines.speaker: Rival

lines.text: Everyone in town has done the sum. Everyone got it right. That's the problem.
lines.say: [cool, slow, each sentence its own beat, the last one bitter and amused] Everyone in town has done the sum. Everyone got it right. That's the problem.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The one who stops first loses to the one who doesn't. In the model, knowing the trap is there gets nobody out of it, and more competition and better machines make it worse. Still unchecked. Same napkin.
lines.say: [grim, exact, a trap described from inside it, the last two words flat] The one who stops first loses to the one who doesn't. In the model, knowing the trap is there gets nobody out of it, and more competition and better machines make it worse. Still unchecked. Same napkin.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The pings stop. Nobody in town can buy a car, so the boss can't pay for five hundred shifts.
lines.say: [hushed, after the silence, the second sentence heavier than the first] The pings stop. Nobody in town can buy a car, so the boss can't pay for five hundred shifts.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Problem two. You own every machine in town, and you're the one going broke.
lines.say: [dry, a card laid down, a dark laugh on the last four words] Problem two. You own every machine in town, and you're the one going broke.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you type CUSTOMER.
lines.say: [sly, quick, the comment section's idea, the last word deadpan] So you type CUSTOMER.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Its card is your card. The till rings, your pocket empties, and the pie just sits there.
lines.say: [deadpan, a joke performed slowly, a sigh on the pie] Its card is your card. The till rings, your pocket empties, and the pie just sits there.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A machine never calls in sick. It never eats the pie, either.
lines.say: [fond, rueful, a complete thought, the last word soft] A machine never calls in sick. It never eats the pie, either.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plant boss: Prices will fall. They'll buy then.
lines.say: [hopeful, a little desperate, coat on in the doorway] Prices will fall. They'll buy then.
lines.speaker: Plant boss

lines.text: The plant halves its cars. The bread costs pennies. SALE in every window. Nothing moves.
lines.say: [quick, a montage counted off, then dead flat on the last two words] The plant halves its cars. The bread costs pennies. SALE in every window. Nothing moves.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A price is never zero. A wage can be.
lines.say: [cold, precise, the second sentence slower] A price is never zero. A wage can be.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you give the money back.
lines.say: [brisk, a shrug, a new idea with a little hope in it] So you give the money back.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You write every resident a cheque. Every month, out of the rent.
lines.say: [generous, brisk, a pen moving fast] You write every resident a cheque. Every month, out of the rent.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It's been done, more or less. Alaska has paid its residents a yearly cheque out of oil money since 1982, about twelve hundred dollars this year.
lines.say: [fair, plain, a fact offered honestly] It's been done, more or less. Alaska has paid its residents a yearly cheque out of oil money since nineteen eighty-two, about twelve hundred dollars this year.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The stools fill for a week.
lines.say: [bright, relieved, then a shadow on the last three words] The stools fill for a week.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then the money goes into tills with robots behind them, and the owners spend it on more machines, because a machine is still cheaper than a person.
lines.say: [tracing a loop with a finger, quickening, a weary laugh on the last clause] Then the money goes into tills with robots behind them, and the owners spend it on more machines, because a machine is still cheaper than a person.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It pays the bills. It doesn't change the sum.
lines.say: [even, kind, then firm on the second sentence] It pays the bills. It doesn't change the sum.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Who keeps the money? The hairdresser. The plumber. The bar with the live band.
lines.say: [curious, then a detective naming them, a smile on the band] Who keeps the money? The hairdresser. The plumber. The bar with the live band.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A string quartet takes four musicians and the same time it took two centuries ago, and their pay keeps rising, so live music gets dearer against everything a machine makes.
lines.say: [warm, a little wonder in the quartet, then dry on the last clause] A string quartet takes four musicians and the same time it took two centuries ago, and their pay keeps rising, so live music gets dearer against everything a machine makes.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your old waitress is the hairdresser's apprentice now. She charges triple. She waves.
lines.say: [amused, admiring, a laugh on triple, fond on the wave] Your old waitress is the hairdresser's apprentice now. She charges triple. She waves.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And then the town comes for the machines.
lines.say: [low, a drumbeat, the last word heavy] And then the town comes for the machines.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Nobody can bring themselves to hit a smiling face.
lines.say: [hushed, a held breath let out, half a laugh of relief] Nobody can bring themselves to hit a smiling face.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It's been tried. Between 1811 and 1816, English textile workers called Luddites smashed machines in raids on mills. They never had to look one in the face.
lines.say: [storyteller, plain on the fact, the last sentence slow and pointed] It's been tried. Between eighteen eleven and eighteen sixteen, English textile workers called Luddites smashed machines in raids on mills. They never had to look one in the face.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plant boss: Smash ours, and the plant two towns over makes the cars. The board meets Friday noon.
lines.say: [grave, tired, a folder under his arm, the deadline flat] Smash ours, and the plant two towns over makes the cars. The board meets Friday noon.
lines.speaker: Plant boss

lines.text: Problem three.
lines.say: [dry, a third card laid down, the trap closing on the last word] Problem three.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Marco: I used to make that burger.
lines.say: [quiet, wounded, looking at the plate a long moment] I used to make that burger.
lines.speaker: Marco

lines.text: Every owner in town was right to do it. So how can the whole town be wrong?
lines.say: [puzzled, honest, the question asked for real, slow] Every owner in town was right to do it. So how can the whole town be wrong?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Smash them, and the plant leaves and the town keeps its pride. Keep them, and the plant stays and the town keeps nothing else.
lines.say: [measured, two hands weighing, the last two words bleak] Smash them, and the plant leaves and the town keeps its pride. Keep them, and the plant stays and the town keeps nothing else.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And you remember the one thing the app told you to remember.
lines.say: [a slow smile, a secret surfacing, the last word a whisper] And you remember the one thing the app told you to remember.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rival: Mine too? All eight?
lines.say: [panicked, shouting, running past the window] Mine too? All eight?
lines.speaker: Rival

lines.text: Too far. Cheap was a trap. Dear is just a different one: no machines, no plant.
lines.say: [wincing, quick, the last four words flat] Too far. Cheap was a trap. Dear is just a different one: no machines, no plant.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: There. A machine shift now costs whoever rents it the tab its worker would have run up at everyone else's counter.
lines.say: [satisfied, exact, the thumbnail on the napkin, the last clause slow and clear] There. A machine shift now costs whoever rents it the tab its worker would have run up at everyone else's counter.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The app pays it to you. You pay it out as the town's cheque.
lines.say: [plain, brisk, a loop closed with two hands] The app pays it to you. You pay it out as the town's cheque.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In 1920 the economist Pigou argued for taxing the things that hurt your neighbours. The tax carries his name. Yours carries a napkin.
lines.say: [wry, warm, the fact quick, a grin on the napkin] In nineteen twenty the economist Pigou argued for taxing the things that hurt your neighbours. The tax carries his name. Yours carries a napkin.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mayor: And who owns the dial?
lines.say: [sharp, arms folded, a mayor's real question] And who owns the dial?
lines.speaker: Mayor

lines.text: Only you can turn it. So you give away the number. The town writes it, the dial follows the napkin, and you keep the turning.
lines.say: [thoughtful, then decided, each clause a hand passing the pencil, the last word held] Only you can turn it. So you give away the number. The town writes it, the dial follows the napkin, and you keep the turning.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rival: Cheaper to hire a cook.
lines.say: [grudging, a shrug, counting her cooks onto the truck] Cheaper to hire a cook.
lines.speaker: Rival

lines.text: Friday noon. The board votes to stay.
lines.say: [quiet, a breath held, then released on the last word] Friday noon. The board votes to stay.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In the two economists' model the usual fixes fail: a basic income, a wage cut, new firms. What can work, in that model, is a tax on the machine itself. Their fix. Your dial. Still unchecked. Checked by Marco.
lines.say: [clear, a verdict read with pride, honest on the caveat, a grin on the last three words] In the two economists' model the usual fixes fail: a basic income, a wage cut, new firms. What can work, in that model, is a tax on the machine itself. Their fix. Your dial. Still unchecked. Checked by Marco.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You're still the richest person in town. You just stopped being its only customer.
lines.say: [warm, a win, the second sentence slower and sly] You're still the richest person in town. You just stopped being its only customer.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Plant boss: Still cheaper than a cook?
lines.say: [mouth full, teasing, a burger in his hand] Still cheaper than a cook?
lines.speaker: Plant boss

lines.text: Tomorrow, when you pay for lunch, watch where the money goes. It isn't leaving. It's on its way back round.
lines.say: [close, to you, a lesson handed over gently, the last word drawn out] Tomorrow, when you pay for lunch, watch where the money goes. It isn't leaving. It's on its way back round.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That part's true too. In 2025 Visa said AI agents had already completed real purchases for shoppers, in pilot trials.
lines.say: [hushed, a little spooked, the fact quick and plain] That part's true too. In twenty twenty-five Visa said AI agents had already completed real purchases for shoppers, in pilot trials.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So, who do you think paid for that burger? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have turned the dial, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [bright, direct, a dare on the question, a grin on the last four words] So, who do you think paid for that burger? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have turned the dial, hit like and subscribe.
lines.speaker: narrator
